title: SLO cost-aware capacity safeguard playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the operational pattern we use at Redwood to protect SLOs while preventing uncontrolled cost growth. It ties SLOs, error budgets, and capacity planning to pricing signals so on-call engineers and automation can make safe trade-offs during incidents and sustained load. The goal is to keep customer-facing reliability within agreed SLOs while avoiding catastrophic billing overruns.

Scope
-----
- Applies to hosted inference API, dedicated capacity pools, and cross-region routing policies.
- Covers the lifecycle: detection (telemetry), decision (human or automation), action (throttle/fallback/evict/scale), and post-incident review (cost and reliability reconciliation).
- Not a replacement for individual service runbooks; it supplements them with cost-aware controls.

Owner and stakeholders
----------------------
- Playbook owner: eng-sre (primary contact: Asha Patel).
- Stakeholders: eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, finance, product-ops, customer-success.
- Escalation: follow standard on-call escalation; notify Finance on any action that is expected to change monthly spend > 10%.

Key principles
--------------
1) Safety-first for user experience: preserve SLOs for core API surfaces (text.generation, chat, embeddings) where customers expect low latency.
2) Cost-aware degradation: when capacity constraints or runaway costs occur, prefer measured, reversible policy changes (priority shaping, model variant fallbacks) rather than blunt denial-of-service.
3) Instrumentation-driven decisions: every automated policy must have a clear telemetry signal, a threshold, and a documented rollback.
4) Evidence-led postmortems: incident reviews must include a cost delta alongside SLO impact and mitigation latency.

SLO and error budget bindings
-----------------------------
- Canonical SLOs (examples):
  - text.generation: 95th p99 latency < 350ms; availability >= 99.9% monthly.
  - embeddings.create: 95th p99 latency < 120ms; availability >= 99.95% monthly.
- Error budget unit: percentage of successful requests or a time window depending on service characteristics.
- Cost budget (new): per-service monthly cost ceiling that maps to error budget posture. Finance and product set default ceilings during onboarding.

Burn rate and cost signal fusion
-------------------------------
We augment conventional error-budget burn-rate checks with a cost-signal: token-cost burn rate (TCBR). TCBR = (observed token spend rate) / (expected baseline token spend rate).
Trigger matrix (examples):
1) TCBR < 2x and error budget burn < 2x: monitor, send automated paging to SRE on-call.
2) TCBR >= 2x or error budget burn >= 3x: execute tier-1 mitigation (non-disruptive): enable request sampling, increase prefix-KV cache share, recommend quantized model variant for compatible tenants.
3) TCBR >= 4x or error budget burn >= 6x: execute tier-2 mitigation (degradations allowed): token-priority shaping, per-tenant rate limits, soft-eviction of low-priority workloads.
4) Cost ceiling breach or TCBR >= 8x: emergency mode — apply pre-approved emergency throttles and notify Product + Finance; require post-incident CFO sign-off if action persists beyond 6 hours.

Operational actions and runbook steps
-----------------------------------
Each action below lists preconditions, steps, and verification.

1) Tier-1: Non-disruptive optimizations
Preconditions: TCBR >= 2x or error-budget-burn relatively high but no immediate SLO loss.
Steps:
  - Command: redwoodctl telemetry analyze --service <svc> --window 15m --metrics token_rate,error_budget_burn
  - Apply: enable adaptive batching for model family: redwoodctl service update <svc> --enable-adaptive-batching
  - Increase prefix cache allocation: redwoodctl runtime cache set --service <svc> --prefix-shares +10%
  - Notify: create a ticket in #oncall with details and executed steps.
Verification: token_rate reduced or latency maintained; continue monitoring for 30m.

2) Tier-2: Measured degradations
Preconditions: sustained TCBR >= 4x or error budget burn >= 6x for 30m.
Steps:
  - Apply per-tenant priority shaping policy: 
    redwoodctl routing set-priority --service <svc> --tenant-file priority.json
  - Example priority.json: 
    {"tenants": [{"id":"tenant-123","priority":"high"},{"id":"tenant-789","priority":"low"}],"default":"standard"}
  - Rollout fallback models for low-priority tenants: redwoodctl rollout apply --service <svc> --selector "priority=low" --model-model-v2-quantized:1.0
  - Temporary rate-limit for non-critical endpoints: redwoodctl rate-limit set --svc <svc> --path "/debug/*" --rps 5
Verification: monitor p50/p95 latencies for high-priority tenants; ensure low-priority error rates remain within documentation.

3) Emergency mode: cost ceiling breach
Preconditions: automated detection or manual CFO/CTO approval when spend > configured ceiling.
Steps (must be approved by on-call lead):
  - Execute emergency throttle: redwoodctl emergency throttle --service <svc> --global-rps 50 --reason "cost-ceiling-breach"
  - Enable fallback region routing: redwoodctl routing set-fallback --service <svc> --region eu-central-1
  - Notify multi-channel (PagerDuty escalation, #finance-alerts, CS lead).
  - Open temporary incident document using template: /incidents/new-cost-safeguard.md
Verification: spend enters acceptable range; SLOs for core customers must be verified immediately after throttle. Document all approvals.

Capacity planning tie-ins
------------------------
- Onboarding checklist must include: expected token volume, model families, acceptable latency, monthly cost ceiling.
- Capacity runway calculation (simple formula): required_gpu_hours = expected_tokens * tokens_per_request_avg * model_efficiency_factor / (gpu_tokens_per_hour)
- Reserve buckets: critical, standard, best-effort. Each tenant is assigned a reservation class during onboarding.
- Autoscale policies should be cost-aware: scale-up thresholds are gated by short-term TCBR and monthly pro-rata spend.

Tooling and telemetry requirements
--------------------------------
Minimum telemetry to support this playbook:
- token_rate (per service, per tenant) — 1s granularity for edge services, 60s for batch.
- cost_rate (USD/min) — derived from token consumption and per-model price table.
- error_budget_burn (ratio) — rolling 1h, 24h window.
- latency quantiles (p50, p95, p99).
- model_variant_usage and kv_cache_hit_rate.

Suggested dashboards (examples):
- Cost vs SLO heatmap: Y axis = error_budget_burn, X axis = cost_rate.
- Tenant exposure dashboard: shows top 50 tenants by token spend and their priority class.

Automated policy examples (JSON)
-------------------------------
Sample routing/mitigation policy that can be loaded into runtime: 
{"policy_name": "cost-safeguard-default",
  "triggers": [{"metric":"tcbr","op":">=","value":4,"duration":"00:30:00"}],
  "actions": ["apply_priority_shaping","fallback_low_priority_models","notify_oncall"]
}

Incident review addendum (evidence required)
------------------------------------------
Every incident where cost-aware actions are executed must include the following in the post-incident report:
- timeline of telemetry (token_rate, cost_rate, error_budget_burn) with 1-minute resolution around action windows.
- list of actions executed, timestamps, executor (automation or individual).
- cost delta: estimated spend avoided or incurred during action window (USD before & after).
- customer impact matrix: customers affected and mitigation applied.
- lessons learned and permanent mitigations proposed.

Runbook checklists for on-call
-----------------------------
Pre-incident (runbook preparation):
1) Confirm SLO ownership and contact roster.
2) Verify cost ceiling for services on shift.
3) Confirm dashboard access and alert routing.
During incident: use the checklist below in order, escalations only jump steps if explicitly allowed in service-specific runbooks.
1) Triage: execute telemetry analyze command and attach graphs to incident.
2) Inform: page SILVER (SRE) if TCBR >=2x; escalate to GOLD (engineering lead) if TCBR >=4x.
3) Apply Tier-1 actions and monitor for 30m.
4) If no improvement, apply Tier-2 actions and notify Finance.
5) If cost ceiling breach, follow Emergency mode.
Post-incident: compile cost evidence, run retro, and schedule debt ticket if policy gaps found.

Templates and snippets
---------------------
- Priority file example (CSV):
  tenant_id,priority,owner
  tenant-123,high,@alice
  tenant-456,standard,@bob
  tenant-789,low,@ops

- Incident document subject line: "[INCIDENT][cost-safeguard] <service> — <short description> — <date>"

Governance and review cadence
----------------------------
- Quarterly review between Eng-SRE, Finance, and Product to adjust default cost ceilings and service-class mappings.
- Any manual emergency action that remains active > 6 hours requires a post-incident review within 72 hours and CFO acknowledgement for cost changes.

Appendix: quick reference table
------------------------------
| Trigger (approx) | Primary action | Approver | Notification window |
|------------------|----------------|---------|---------------------|
| TCBR >= 2x       | Tier-1 optimizations (batching, cache) | on-call | 15m |
| TCBR >= 4x       | Priority shaping, fallback models | on-call lead | 5m |
| Cost ceiling breach | Emergency throttle & routing | on-call lead + Finance | immediate |

Contacts and escalation anchors
-------------------------------
- Eng-SRE on-call: use PagerDuty A rota.
- Finance alert inbox: finance-alerts@redwood.example.com
- Product escalation: product-ops@redwood.example.com
